architecture.goal: Replace the current workflow with a smaller Express state machine that preserves phase-3 behavior while removing duplicated branches, runtime type mismatches, and asymmetric closure logic.
runtime_shape: Producer Lambda queries one dispatch slot and publishes one SQS FIFO message per work item
EventBridge Pipe consumes the FIFO queue with batchSize = 1 and starts the Express workflow synchronously
The workflow starts by normalizing the single-message batch payload and enriching TTL metadata through one bootstrap Lambda
The workflow acquires idempotency, claims the pending record, invokes the consumer Lambda, and closes through one success path or one of three explicit failure paths
The workflow owns all final writes to tapi-results, tapi-idempotency, and tapi-pending-records
explicit_non_goals: Changing the producer routing model or SQS FIFO provider isolation
Changing the consumer into a persistence owner
Adding replay tooling, dashboards, or manual repair automation in this refactor
Changing the scheduler topology or dispatch-slot model
design_principles: Keep one state per real responsibility; avoid branch-specific duplicate states when a shared state is sufficient
Preserve a single canonical workflow context after bootstrap and never switch root shape again
Use string fields only where Step Functions service integrations require string numerics, and keep native numbers elsewhere
Persist one uniform result contract where responseBody is always a string payload

module_boundaries.responsibility: Read one FIFO message, wrap it in the current single-item batch shape, and invoke the Express workflow synchronously.
Convert the batch-shaped Pipe input into the canonical workflow object, normalize optional payload and headers, and compute TTL strings.
Own operational orchestration: idempotency claim, pending claim, retry policy, failure classification routing, and final closure persistence.
Perform the provider API call and return a success result or throw classified business errors without writing DynamoDB state.

hard_rules: Only TTL inputs are allowed to stay as string numerics in the workflow context.
All result-table numeric attributes must be written from pre-normalized string numerics under $.persistence.*Text, never by applying stringAt() directly to raw numeric nodes.
All result-table responseBody values must be strings, including failure rows.
The workflow must not mix DynamoDB String and Map types for the same logical field across branches.

workflow_design.state_strategy: Use one bootstrap state, two claim states, one consumer state, one success-persistence preparation state, one success persistence state, three failure-normalization states, one shared failure-persistence preparation state, one shared failure persistence state, one shared idempotency-failed state, one shared pending-failed state, and one duplicate terminal state.

states.name: BootstrapWorkflowInput
states.responsibility: Flatten the one-item batch input, normalize payload and headers to empty objects, and compute idempotency/results TTL strings.
states.reason_to_keep_lambda: Pipe batch root shape and TTL computation are the only remaining places where a small Lambda removes complexity from the workflow definition.

states.name: AcquireIdempotencyLock
states.responsibility: Create an IN_PROGRESS idempotency record with condition attribute_not_exists(idempotencyKey).

states.name: MarkPendingInProgress
states.responsibility: Move the pending record from PENDING to IN_PROGRESS with a conditional update.

states.name: RollbackIdempotencyLock
states.responsibility: Remove the just-created idempotency lock when the pending record could not be claimed.

states.name: InvokeConsumerLambda
states.responsibility: Call the pure business consumer with workItem only.

states.name: NormalizeTerminalFailure
states.responsibility: Parse the TerminalApiError envelope into NormalizedFailure.
states.output_rule: Keep workItem and workflow untouched, parse $.workflowError.Cause, parse its errorMessage payload, and add normalizedFailure with category TERMINAL and the provider status code.

states.name: NormalizeTransientExhaustedFailure
states.responsibility: Parse the exhausted TransientApiError envelope into NormalizedFailure.
states.output_rule: Keep workItem and workflow untouched, parse $.workflowError.Cause, parse its errorMessage payload, and add normalizedFailure with category TRANSIENT_EXHAUSTED and the provider status code.

states.name: NormalizeTimeoutFailure
states.output_rule: Set normalizedFailure to { statusCode: 504, message: 'Provider execution timed out', category: 'TIMEOUT' }.

states.name: NormalizeUnexpectedFailure
states.responsibility: Map any unclassified workflow or runtime error into NormalizedFailure.
states.output_rule: Set normalizedFailure to { statusCode: 500, message: <workflowError.Cause>, category: 'UNEXPECTED' }.

states.name: PrepareSuccessPersistence
states.responsibility: Derive one persistence sub-object with DynamoDB-safe strings for numeric fields and the final result-row values.
states.output_rule: Add $.persistence with statusCodeText, durationMsText, responseBodyText, processedAt, resultPk, resultSk, and ttlText while preserving workItem, workflow, and consumerResult.

states.name: PersistSuccessResult
states.responsibility: Write the success ResultRecordWrite contract to tapi-results.
states.typing_rule: statusCode, durationMs, and ttl are written via numberFromString from $.persistence.statusCodeText, $.persistence.durationMsText, and $.persistence.ttlText. responseBody is written from $.persistence.responseBodyText.

states.name: PrepareFailurePersistence
states.responsibility: Derive one persistence sub-object with DynamoDB-safe strings for numeric fields and a serialized failure response body.
states.output_rule: Add $.persistence with statusCodeText, durationMsText = '0', responseBodyText = JSON string of failure metadata, processedAt, resultPk, resultSk, and ttlText while preserving workItem, workflow, workflowError, and normalizedFailure.

states.name: PersistFailureResult
states.responsibility: Write one uniform failure ResultRecordWrite contract to tapi-results.
states.typing_rule: statusCode, durationMs, and ttl are written via numberFromString from $.persistence.statusCodeText, $.persistence.durationMsText, and $.persistence.ttlText. responseBody is written from $.persistence.responseBodyText.

states.name: MarkIdempotencyCompleted
states.responsibility: Set the idempotency record to COMPLETED with completedAt timestamp.

states.name: MarkPendingCompleted
states.responsibility: Set the pending record to COMPLETED.

states.name: MarkIdempotencyFailed
states.responsibility: Set the idempotency record to FAILED with failedAt and a reason derived from normalizedFailure.category.

states.name: MarkPendingFailed
states.responsibility: Set the pending record to FAILED.

states.name: DuplicateWorkItem
states.responsibility: Terminate duplicate or no-longer-claimable work without a second consumer invocation.

notes: This state must remain the only place that understands the Pipe batch root shape.
The Lambda output becomes the new root object for the rest of the workflow.
No workflow metadata is sent to the consumer.
The Lambda response must be stored under $.consumerResult via resultPath.
If one Pass state cannot legally reference sibling derived fields in the target implementation, split this into two states: ParseWorkflowErrorEnvelope -> NormalizeTerminalFailure.
If one Pass state cannot legally reference sibling derived fields in the target implementation, split this into two states: ParseWorkflowErrorEnvelope -> NormalizeTransientExhaustedFailure.

If the target implementation cannot use States.JsonToString with an inline object literal in one state, create a small prior Pass state that materializes failureResponseBodyObject and then call States.JsonToString on that object.

clarifications.single_execution_unit: Yes. One state machine execution processes one single work item, which corresponds to one single pending record read by the producer and one single FIFO message consumed by the Pipe.
clarifications.happy_path_summary: If the consumer call returns OK, the workflow writes one row to tapi-results, marks the idempotency row COMPLETED, and marks the pending row COMPLETED.
clarifications.no_bulk_processing_inside_workflow: The workflow never loops through multiple records. Fan-out happens before the workflow, in producer -> SQS FIFO. The state machine handles one record at a time.
clarifications.type_safety_strategy: Every numeric field that will be written to DynamoDB is first converted into a string numeric inside $.persistence.*Text. Every DynamoDB numeric write then reads only from those normalized string fields.

failure_modes_and_edge_handling.handling: Route directly to DuplicateWorkItem and do not invoke the consumer.

failure_modes_and_edge_handling.case: Pending record is missing or not PENDING
failure_modes_and_edge_handling.handling: Delete the just-created idempotency lock, route to DuplicateWorkItem, and do not invoke the consumer.
Persist success, then close idempotency and pending as COMPLETED.
Do not retry. Normalize the failure and close through PersistFailureResult -> MarkIdempotencyFailed -> MarkPendingFailed.
Normalize as TRANSIENT_EXHAUSTED and close through the shared failure closure states.
Normalize as TIMEOUT with statusCode 504 and close through the shared failure closure states.

failure_modes_and_edge_handling.case: Unexpected internal/runtime error occurs after consumer invocation
failure_modes_and_edge_handling.handling: Normalize as UNEXPECTED and close through the shared failure closure states.
Prevented by design: all result writes use a single typed contract and responseBody is always serialized to string.

failure_modes_and_edge_handling.case: Closure-path task fails after a work item is already claimed
failure_modes_and_edge_handling.handling: The implementation must add catch coverage on persistence/closure tasks to route into the unexpected closure path instead of hard-failing the execution and leaving the item silently stuck.

dependency_and_library_decisions.decision: Keep one bootstrap Lambda instead of removing Lambda use entirely from the workflow.
dependency_and_library_decisions.rationale: It collapses batch-root normalization, optional payload/header defaults, and TTL computation into one predictable step and keeps the workflow definition smaller.

dependency_and_library_decisions.decision: Use one shared failure persistence state instead of separate terminal/transient/timeout/unexpected persistence tasks.
dependency_and_library_decisions.rationale: This removes duplicated DynamoDB shapes and reduces the chance of branch drift.

dependency_and_library_decisions.decision: Persist failure responseBody as serialized JSON string, not a DynamoDB map.
dependency_and_library_decisions.rationale: This restores a single result contract compatible with the existing shared types and easier querying.

dependency_and_library_decisions.decision: Preserve Express workflow type and synchronous Pipe invocation.
dependency_and_library_decisions.rationale: This keeps same-provider serialization aligned with the final architecture.

quality_gates: CDK synth tests prove the new workflow topology and the removal of duplicated failure branches.
Unit tests still prove the consumer remains persistence-free and preserves classified error behavior.
Manual AWS execution succeeds for success, terminal, transient exhausted, and unexpected closures using real DynamoDB-backed records.
expected_test_scenarios: A real PENDING record with HTTP 200 closes as COMPLETED and writes one result row with numeric statusCode and durationMs.
A real PENDING record with HTTP 400 closes as FAILED without retry and writes one serialized failure responseBody.
A real PENDING record with HTTP 503 retries, exhausts, and closes as FAILED with category TRANSIENT_EXHAUSTED.
A forced unexpected error in the consumer or workflow closes as FAILED with category UNEXPECTED instead of TransientApiError(0).
A duplicate idempotency key or non-PENDING pending record ends in DuplicateWorkItem without a second consumer invocation.
No success or failure result write uses mixed attribute types for responseBody.

phased_implementation_plan.goal: Remove the current state machine definition and replace it with a clean minimal workflow graph.
tasks: Delete the duplicated parse and persistence branches from the current CDK definition.
Define the new bootstrap, claim, consumer, success, normalized failure, and shared closure states.
Keep the same state machine name and Express configuration unless replacement is required by CloudFormation.
definition_of_done: The workflow graph can be read top-to-bottom without branch-specific duplicated persistence logic.
The success path and all failure paths use the canonical workflow context.

phased_implementation_plan.goal: Make all DynamoDB writes type-safe and uniform.
tasks: Fix numeric persistence so statusCode and durationMs are always written with the correct numeric task helpers.
Serialize failure responseBody to string and remove DynamoDB map writes for results.
Keep ttl persistence as numeric values derived from string TTL inputs.
definition_of_done: A manual success execution no longer fails in PersistSuccessResult.
A manual failure execution no longer writes a branch-specific responseBody type.

phased_implementation_plan.goal: Avoid silent stuck IN_PROGRESS states when post-consumer closure tasks fail.
tasks: Add catch routing on persistence and closure tasks into the unexpected closure path where technically feasible.
Ensure failure to claim pending state rolls back idempotency lock before duplicate termination.
Verify duplicate and stale-claim scenarios do not invoke the consumer.
definition_of_done: The workflow does not hard-fail immediately after a claimed work item without attempting a controlled unexpected closure.

assumptions: The rebuild keeps using the existing workflow bootstrap Lambda rather than replacing TTL computation with a more complex intrinsic-only approach.
The current Step Functions logging configuration remains acceptable for this refactor.
Manual AWS validation will use real DynamoDB-backed records and direct Start execution / start-sync-execution tests as part of acceptance.
